item.title: Well-posedness of a stress-augmented Moore-Gibson-Thompson-type model for thermoviscoelastic evolution in a standard linear solid
item.description: arXiv:2610.31134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This manuscript studies a coupled system of nonlinear parabolic and hyperbolic equations that models thermoviscoelastic materials with explicit internal stress relaxation, $$\begin{cases} \tau u_{ttt} + u_{tt} = (D(\Theta)u_{xt})_x + (C(\Theta)u_x)_x, \\ \Theta_t = \Theta_{xx} + |E(\Theta)u_{xt} + F(\Theta)g_t|^2, \\ \tau g_t + g = D(\Theta)u_{xt} + C(\Theta)u_x. \end{cases}$$ The system arises from a stress-strain constitutive relation of Zener type, where the internal variable $g$ encodes mechanical memory effects. A key feature is the explicit coupling of stress relaxation to the heat equation through the dissipation term, which differs from standard approaches that eliminate $g$ via algebraic substitution. Under the assumptions that $\tau>0$ and that $D,C\in C^2([0,\infty))$ are positive and $E,F\in C^1([0,\infty))$, and for suitably regular initial data, we establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. Under additionally strengthened regularity requirements on the initial data and on $D,C$, this solution is moreover shown to be classical. These results extend a corresponding local strong and classical solvability theory developed for the underlying system without the stress variable $g$ to the present, stress-augmented setting.
item.dc:creator: Torben Fricke

item.title: Grushin spherical harmonics in non-degenerate dimension one
item.description: arXiv:2610.31137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Grushin Laplacian $\Delta_\alpha = \Delta_x +|x|^{2\alpha}\Delta_y $ is a degenerate elliptic operator in $\mathbb{R}^{h+k}$ that degenerates on $\{0\} \times \mathbb{R}^k$. We explicitly compute the Grushin spherical harmonics on the gauge sphere $\{(x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^{h+k} : |x|^{2(\alpha+1)}+(\alpha+1)^2|y|^2=1\}$ and the corresponding spectrum when the non-degenerate dimension $h=1$, a case not covered by the existing literature. The eigenfunctions consist of homogeneous Grushin-harmonic polynomials of degrees $n \equiv 0,1 \pmod{\alpha+1}$, even and odd in the $x$-variable respectively, which can be described in terms of Jacobi polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Bramati, Paolo Luzzini

item.title: Liouville Theorems and Sharp Homogeneity Defects for Weighted Potential Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider \[ \begin{cases} u=K*(|x|^\alpha a_0(x)v^p)&\quad\hbox{in }\mathbb R^n,\\ v=K*(|x|^\beta b_0(x)u^q)&\quad\hbox{in }\mathbb R^n, \end{cases} \] where $n\ge2$, $0<\rho<n$, $p,q>0$, and $\alpha,\beta>-\rho$. The radial kernel is nonincreasing and satisfies $K(r)\asymp r^{\rho-n}$. The coefficients satisfy $0<c_0\le a_0(x),b_0(x)\le C_0$ and $|x|(|\nabla\log a_0(x)|+|\nabla\log b_0(x)|)\le L$. We prove nonexistence if \[ \frac{n+\alpha-\varepsilon_a}{p+1} +\frac{n+\beta-\varepsilon_b}{q+1}>n-\rho+\varepsilon_K, \] where the defects bound the radial logarithmic derivatives. No symmetry, finite-energy condition, or prescribed decay is assumed. The proof combines a localized virial identity with a source-layer pressure estimate whose constants are uniform under centered dilations, including the low-order range $0<\rho\le1$. We also identify the necessary scaling range for existence. For radial weighted Newton systems with unequal powers, we prove that the combined coefficient defect has a sharp, unattained infimum equal to the subcritical gap. A fixed bound on the coefficient ratios forces a strictly larger defect, whereas suitable coefficient--solution pairs approach the threshold with excess at most $C/\log M$. In the scalar Newton case, the threshold is explicit and the approximating family converges, after normalization, to an explicit critical weighted profile. The sharpness results concern the Newton kernel; no corresponding construction is asserted for general fractional kernels.
item.dc:creator: Shengbing Deng, Bo Zhang

item.title: Sharp quantitative stability of the Ashbaugh--Benguria inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.31223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sharp quantitative stability of the Ashbaugh--Benguria inequality on bounded convex domains in $\mathbb R^n$. After volume and centroid normalization, the eigenvalue-ratio deficit controls the squared $H^{-1/2}(\mathbb S^{n-1})$ norm of the radial displacement from the unit sphere. This yields the optimal exponent $5/2$ for the Fraenkel asymmetry and, for small deficits, the optimal exponent $(n+4)/2$ for the normalized Hausdorff distance. All three exponents are sharp even among smooth strictly convex domains whose principal curvatures lie in $[1/2,2]$. In particular, the quadratic Fraenkel-asymmetry estimate proposed by Brasco and De Philippis (2017, Open Problem 7.65) fails. We also determine the optimal stability exponents under higher-order radial regularity bounds.
item.dc:creator: Long-Han Huang, Yuxuan Zhou, Wenming Zou

item.title: Sparse power spectrum for passive scalars under Pierrehumbert flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.31241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the long-time Fourier distribution of driven passive scalars transported by an incompressible alternating shear flow (the Pierrehumbert flow) subjected to IID random phase shifts, in the regime of strong shear-strength. With a novel and self-contained proof, we establish (i) a quantitative version of the cumulative Batchelor's law; (ii) quantitative negative regularity mixing estimates; and (iii) a strong form of `sparsity' -- unevenness in the distribution of Fourier mass in radial sectors in frequency space. Our method uses the strong shear-strength assumption to handle a purely deterministic scalar driving term.
item.dc:creator: Alex Blumenthal, William Cooperman

item.title: Chaos of Caputo derivative
item.description: arXiv:2610.31255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study bounded realizations of Caputo differentiation on coefficient Banach spaces of fractional power series. The main contribution is an explicit quantitative analysis of local approximation and periodic reconstruction. We determine the least possible simultaneous error in the initial displacement and the prescribed target. The optimal value is attained, and a minimizing perturbation is given explicitly. We also solve the exact-arrival problem and establish uniqueness of its least-norm solution. These formulas provide computable approximation times and identify the sharp threshold for hypercyclicity, mixing and Devaney chaos. Every periodic point is described by a finite block whose geometric repetition yields exact norm formulas. The resulting approximations attain any prescribed sufficiently large minimal period near any given vector. For distinct positive powers, a simultaneous block construction gives quantitative error estimates and the same sharp threshold for disjoint mixing. Compact embeddings relate the Banach realizations to the Mittag-Leffler-Caputo Fr\'echet space. They also exhibit dense stable invariant subspaces inside chaotic realizations. The local approximation condition is a norm formulation of classical transitivity. Its quantitative evaluation, together with explicit periodic and simultaneous reconstruction, provides the central results of the study.
item.dc:creator: El-Mahdi Nafia, Aziz El Ghazouani, M'hamed El Omari

item.title: A New Minimax Theorem for a Class of $C^1$-Functionals
item.description: arXiv:2610.31262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a new abstract minimax theorem for obtaining ground-state critical points of a class of \(C^{1}\)-functionals. The central feature of this class is that the associated Nehari set is not necessarily a differentiable manifold, but is homeomorphic to a (possibly non-complete) submanifold of the unit sphere. This occurs for functionals whose fibering maps \(t \mapsto I(tu)\) possess a unique global maximum point only when \(u\) belongs to an open cone in the underlying Banach space. A lower semicontinuous boundary barrier, which may be finite, controls minimizing sequences near the boundary of the spherical cone. As a consequence, we provide a general minimax characterization of the ground-state energy level. Elliptic applications complement existing results and include superlinear and quasilinear problems with finite barriers, including thresholds depending on the profile of a first eigenfunction and its gradient.
item.dc:creator: Denilson S. Pereira, Jo\~ao R. Santos J\'unior, Jo\~ao F. F. Silva

item.title: Radial $\Phi^4$ models in supercritical regimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.31267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the $\Phi^4_d$ measure under radial symmetry on the unit ball, formally given by $$d\rho(u) = \frac 1 Z \exp\Big( - \frac 14 \int_{B_1} |u|^4 dx - \frac 12 \int_{B_1} |\nabla u|^2 dx\Big) d u, $$ where $u$ is restricted to radially symmetric functions with 0 boundary conditions. We prove that for every dimension $d$, there exists such a measure, which is concentrated on $L^p(B_1)$ for every $p < \frac{2d}{d-2}$ (for every $p < \infty$ if $d \le 2$). Furthermore, we show that these measures are not Gaussian, and when $d \ge 4$, they are singular with respect to the underlying Gaussian measure. We achieve this result by first defining the measure $\rho^+_\delta[\lambda]$ on the shell $\{\delta \le |x| \le 1\}$, $0 < \delta < 1$, with a boundary condition on the sphere of radius $\delta$ of the form $u|_{\{|x| = \delta\}} = \lambda$. Then we prove that this measure satisfies a variational formula, and use it to show moment bounds which are uniform in the boundary value $\lambda$. A crucial ingredient in this argument is the fact that every solution of the elliptic equation $-\Delta u + u^3 = 0$ on the annulus $\{ \delta \le |x| \le 1 \}$ satisfies uniform bounds inside the domain, independently of the boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Tadahiro Oh, Leonardo Tolomeo, Nikolay Tzvetkov, Yuzhao Wang

item.title: Sharp stability for the Talenti inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.31369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a sharp quantitative version of the Talenti rearrangement inequality. Specifically, we show that, for any $p\in [1;+\infty]$, for any $f\in L^\infty(\Omega),\, f\geq 0,\, f\not\equiv 0$, for any open set $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with finite volume, the solution $u_{f,\Omega}$ to $-\Delta u_{f,\Omega}=f,\, u_{f,\Omega} \in W^{1,2}_0(\Omega)$, satisfies, in dimension $d\geq 1$, $\Vert u_{f^\sharp,\Omega^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(\Omega^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,\Omega}\Vert_{L^p(\Omega)}\gtrsim \alpha(\Omega)^2+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}\mathscr A(f,z)^2$ and, in dimension 1, $ \Vert u_{f^\sharp,\Omega^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(\Omega^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,\Omega}\Vert_{L^p(\Omega)}\gtrsim \alpha(\Omega)+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}}\mathscr A(f,z)^2$ where $\alpha(\Omega)$ denotes the Fraenkel asymmetry of $\Omega$, $\mathscr A(f,z)$ a weighted asymmetry of $f$ with respect to some center $z$ and $\Omega^\sharp$ (resp. $f^\sharp$) is the Schwarz rearrangement of $\Omega$ (resp. of $f$). In dimension $d\geq 2$, this estimate implies $ \Vert u_{f^\sharp,\Omega^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(\Omega^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,\Omega}\Vert_{L^p(\Omega)}\gtrsim \alpha(\Omega)^2+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}\Vert f-f^\sharp(\cdot-z)\Vert_{L^1}^2.$ Our result sharpens and extends recent quantitative versions, and does not rely on shape differentiation arguments, but on a generalisation of the quantitative Saint-Venant inequality.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Acampora, Jimmy Lamboley, Idriss Mazari-Fouquer

item.title: Concavity of the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck torsion function on centered ellipses and its failure on convex domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.31405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $u$ be the torsion function of a bounded domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator, that is, the solution of $-\Delta u + x\cdot\nabla u = 1$ in $\Omega$ with $u=0$ on the boundary. We prove that for every $n\ge2$ there are bounded, centrally symmetric domains whose torsion function is not concave. These domains have boundary with a flat piece and can be smoothed so that the boundary is $C^\infty$, strictly convex with principal curvatures bounded below by a positive constant, while keeping the torsion function not concave. In contrast, the torsion function for every ellipse centered at the origin is concave, and for every ball centered at the origin we prove the sharp bound $D^2u\leq-\frac{1}{n}I$. The ellipse result follows by deformation from the disk, using a boundary flux estimate and third-order boundary identities to exclude a first zero eigenvalue of the Hessian.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Hien Nguyen, Alina Stancu

item.title: A hybrid finite-volume scheme with learned rational reconstructions and exact nonlocal fluxes for the space-fractional Burgers equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.31419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On coarse grids, fronts of fractional conservation laws can be narrower than one cell, while the flux through each face depends on the whole domain. For the forced space-fractional Burgers equation, we write the finite-volume defect exactly, with the Riesz flux acting as a nonlocal interface flux. Our proposed closure, NRC, is decoder-only, since the encoder is the exact cell-average projection and a small network only maps cell averages to a sub-cell reconstruction. The decoder adds rational atoms with learned complex poles to a trigonometric histopolant, preserves every cell average, and has closed-form advective and Riesz fluxes. We prove that the scheme conserves mass for every value of the weights and that the learned sub-grid flux has a dipole tail. On 64 cells, NRC reaches a median test error of 0.0308% over three seeds, against 0.431% for WENO5-Z and 0.153% for a black-box flux correction. Ablations show that the exact global operator, the projection and the sub-grid Riesz flux carry most of this gain, and most sub-cell fronts carry a deep learned pole within a quarter cell. NRC keeps its advantage over WENO5-Z under shifts of the order and the forcing and, when trained on several diffusivities, under the tested diffusivity shifts by factors from 0.6 to 2.5 in the median over seeds. From 32 to 128 cells, NRC stays an order of magnitude more accurate than WENO5-Z on the same grid. This gain lies in accuracy per degree of freedom and in an interpretable closure.
item.dc:creator: Zeyuan Song, Zheyu Jiang

item.title: A special Hardy estimate in the axisymmetric swirl problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.31435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the proof of Dongyi Wei's logarithmic circulation criterion. A trace estimate specific to $\nabla(u_r/r)$ replaces a generic squared-swirl form bound by one with one logarithm rather than two. Repeating the coupled $J$--$\Omega$ energy and comparison argument then gives a proposed threshold of order $(\log D)^{-5/4}$. Under the hypotheses stated below, the proof is intended to establish regularity when $|r u_\theta|\le C|\log r|^{-\alpha}$ uniformly near the axis with $\alpha>5/4$, and at $\alpha=5/4$ with an absolute sufficiently small coefficient. Every analytic step, including the cutoff core and exterior terms, is included for independent checking.
item.dc:creator: Daoguo Zhou

item.title: Boundary regularity of $k$-Hessian eigenfunctions
item.description: arXiv:2610.31445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove smoothness up to the boundary for $k$-Hessian eigenfunctions on smooth bounded uniformly convex domains when $2\leq k<n$. This resolves an open problem in the regularity theory of degenerate fully nonlinear elliptic equations and extends the boundary smoothness theorem for Monge--Amp\`ere eigenfunctions. In contrast to the Monge--Amp\`ere case, the linearized $k$-Hessian operator remains uniformly elliptic up to the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Guohuan Qiu, Jin Yan

item.title: On exact solutions to three-dimensional Yukawa lattice model and BCC to FCC phase transitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.31456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the global minimizers of the three-dimensional Yukawa lattice energy at every fixed density. At unit covolume, BCC is the unique minimizer below a transition parameter $\kappa_*\approx1.7179218684699$, FCC is the unique minimizer above it, and exactly these two lattice classes minimize at the transition. Mathematically, denote the Yukawa potential and the energy per particle under this potential by \[ v_\kappa(r)=\frac{e^{-\kappa r}}r,\qquad E_\kappa(L)=\frac12\sum_{v\in L\setminus\{0\}} \frac{e^{-\kappa|v|}}{|v|}. \] Then, \[ \arg\min_{|L|=1}E_\kappa(L)= \begin{cases} \hbox{BCC lattice},&0<\kappa<\kappa_*, \hbox{BCC or FCC lattice},&\kappa=\kappa_*, \hbox{FCC lattice},&\kappa>\kappa_*. \end{cases} \] As a consequence, the zero-screening comparison recovers the unique BCC minimum for the renormalized Coulomb energy.
item.dc:creator: Senping Luo, Juncheng Wei

item.title: Uniform coarse ellipticity, $A_2$ weights, and boundary regularity
item.description: arXiv:2610.31463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study symmetric divergence form elliptic equations with measurable coefficients that may be degenerate and unbounded, under a uniform bound on the coarse ellipticity ratio over all ambient cubes and scales. We prove that uniform coarse ellipticity and classical $A_2$ weighted ellipticity define incomparable coefficient classes. For every admissible choice of coarse parameters, we construct a scalar weight with a logarithmically corrected, locally integrable singularity along a product Cantor set. Its codimension is chosen according to the upper coarse discount exponent, and the resulting coefficient satisfies the uniform coarse condition but is comparable to no $A_2$ weight. Conversely, an explicit $A_2$ weight fails the coarse condition for every admissible parameter choice. Under uniform coarse ellipticity we give a direct PDE treatment of boundary regularity in the approximable energy realization. Using coarse interior estimates, we prove boundary decay and solvability of the continuous Dirichlet problem in bounded NTA domains. An almost-positivity argument, with energy approximation and boundary testing justified, yields boundary Harnack and H\"older continuity of quotients of positive solutions with common zero boundary values. The argument requires no additional energy Sobolev inequality and avoids the construction of Green functions. Further examples distinguish uniform coarse control from finite coefficient moments and from coercivity on $\mathrm L^2(\mathrm{d} x)$. We also record interior H\"older estimates and continuity criteria under nonuniform control along nested scales.
item.dc:creator: Kaj Nystr\"om

item.title: Asymptotic observable symmetry for spacetime observability of waves I: The disc
item.description: arXiv:2610.31477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on the spacetime observable symmetry discovered in NWX (2025), we introduce asymptotic observable symmetry (AOS) for the wave equation. Its central object is a family of generated approximate velocities constructed from fixed profiles, carrying the same propagation-induced symmetry at different scales and asymptotically realized by exact waves. We investigate AOS on the disc through radial propagation and reflection. This gives a family of spacetime measurable observation sets satisfying the essential spacetime measurable geometric control condition for a fixed positive observation time. However, the observability inequality fails on each of these fixed sets.
item.dc:creator: Shengquan Xiang

item.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations with slender bodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.31480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study the convergence of solutions of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by slender bodies placed on a fixed periodic grid of size $2\epsilon$ as the size of the bodies goes to zero and the number of bodies goes to infinity. We assume that the width $b_\epsilon$ of the bodies vanishes faster than the length $a_\epsilon$ of the particles. We identify the critical scaling regimes for $a_\epsilon$ and $b_\epsilon$ and prove that in this case the system is effectively described by the Brinkman equations.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Hadr\'e, Richard M. H\"ofer

item.title: Liouville-type theorems and perturbation uniqueness for stationary incompressible MHD with directional fractional dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2610.31517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Liouville-type theorems for stationary solutions of the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics equations in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with directional fractional dissipation $(-\partial_i^2)^{\alpha}u$ and $(-\partial_j^2)^{\beta}b$, where $n\ge 2$ and $0<\alpha,\beta\le 1$. We prove that $u\equiv b\equiv 0$ by assuming that $u\in L^{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $b\in L^{q,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, with suitable conditions on $p$ and $q$. The proof uses a localized fractional energy identity and does not assume finiteness of the global homogeneous Sobolev energy. The method also applies to the case of full fractional dissipation. For the system with common-directional fractional dissipation, we prove stationary uniqueness for compactly supported perturbations of arbitrary smooth transverse shear backgrounds when $0<\alpha,\beta<1$. We also establish a quantitative uniqueness criterion for perturbations of backgrounds with bounded gradients that are not necessarily compactly supported, for all $0<\alpha,\beta\le 1$, assuming directional localization.
item.dc:creator: Yong Zeng

item.title: A spectral multiplier theorem for fractional Hardy operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.31532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the fractional Laplacian with added critical or subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator. We prove a H\"ormander spectral multiplier theorem, i.e., the boundedness of sufficiently smooth multipliers of these Hardy operators on Lebesgue spaces. The range of admissible Lebesgue exponents is optimal, but the smoothness assumption is probably not. The proof combines the Helffer--Sj\"ostrand formula with a quantitative Jaffard lemma for operator-valued matrices.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Merz

item.title: Boltzmann Equation and Hard Sphere Gas with Singular Initial Data: Well-posedness, Kinetic Limit, and Weak Stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.31570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a local well-posedness theory for the spatially inhomogeneous 3-d Boltzmann equation with hard sphere cross-section, accommodating a class of large initial data. This class is an interpolation between the space $L_{x}^{\infty}L_v^{1}$ and $L_{v}^1L_{x}^{\infty}$ (with weight in $v$). It is notable for including data that can have infinite $L_{x,v}^\infty$-norm, entropy density. The core idea of the proof is a homogenization method based on collision geometries. As a key application, we prove the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with initial data in this space, having certain extra conditions. This is the first proof on the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with singular initial data. We also derive weak stability estimates of Boltzmann equation and hard sphere gas within the same functional spaces.
item.dc:creator: Chenjiayue Qi

item.title: A Sharp Gradient Harnack Estimate for the Lane--Emden System
item.description: arXiv:2610.31584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a sharp pointwise gradient estimate for positive entire classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system when one of the exponents lies below the Serrin exponent $n/(n-2)$. The estimate generalizes the positivity of the scalar curvature of the associated conformal metric in the biharmonic case $q=1$. The coefficient in the estimate is optimal on the critical hyperbola.
item.dc:creator: Sanghoon Lee, Kui Li, Juncheng Wei

item.title: Sharp fractional Hardy--Maz'ya remainders on half-spaces: angular reduction and energy stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.31595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $d\geq2$, $0<s<1$, $p>1$, and $\tau>0$, we study the sharp half-space remainder \[ [u]_{s,p,+}^p-\mathcal D_{d,s,p}\int_{\mathbb R^d_+}x_d^{-sp}|u|^p\,dx \geq\Lambda_{d,s,p,\tau}\int_{\mathbb R^d_+} \frac{x_d^{\tau-sp}|u|^p}{(x_{d-1}^2+x_d^2)^{\tau/2}}\,dx. \] We first obtain exact dimensional and angular reductions by an $L^p$ contraction. For $p=2$, we identify the planar sharp coefficient with the simple first eigenvalue of a singular angular operator with compact resolvent. We prove a ground-state representation and a two-sided estimate for the sharp deficit. These give quantitative stability and a Fourier--Mellin energy criterion for extremizing sequences in all dimensions. For the distance with multiplier $h(\xi)=\min\{\xi^2,1\}$, the best planar stability coefficient is not attained and is strictly smaller than the quadratic dispersion coefficient. The minimizing frequencies are nonzero when $\tau=2$ and $s$ is close to one. Finally, we prove normalized local limits for the sharp quadratic constant, each fixed fiber eigenvalue, and the dispersion coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Shengbing Deng, Dehong Yang

item.title: Non-uniqueness for the forced one-dimensional Vlasov-Poisson equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.31629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove non-uniqueness for the forced one-dimensional Vlasov-Poisson equation on the whole space. More precisely, for every finite $p$, we construct a nonnegative ion density, smooth for positive times, and a source $S\in C([0,1];L^1(\R^2))$ with $S(0)=0$, for which there exist two distinct nonnegative distributional solutions $f_\pm\in C([0,1];L^1(\R^2))$ with the same zero initial datum and with spatial densities bounded in $L^p(\R)$ uniformly in time. The result is sharp in terms of the integrability of the spatial densities: our solutions have Lipschitz electric fields, and we show that in this class uniqueness holds as soon as the spatial density is bounded.
item.dc:creator: Mikaela Iacobelli

item.title: Quantitative constructive representation of the KdV flow in $H^3$ via $L^2$-energy-preserving centered-difference Chernoff approximations and Picard iteration
item.description: arXiv:2610.31634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a constructive representation of the solution of the KdV equation $u_t=-u_{xxx}+6uu_x$ on $\mathbb R$ for real initial data in $H^3(\mathbb R)$. The approximations couple an exact, unitary centered-difference Chernoff product for the Airy group with a skew-symmetric discretization of the quadratic term, and are computed by Picard iteration; they preserve the $L^2$ norm exactly, as does the limit. A two-mesh Cauchy argument shows that the whole sequence converges in $C([0,T];H^2)$, at rate $O(n^{-\frac{2(s-2)}5})$ for $H^s$ data ($3\leq s\leq 7$), and in $L^2$ at rate $O(n^{-6/5})$ for $H^3$ data. This scheme, to the best of our knowledge, is novel and is of independent interest. As a by-product we obtain existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, Lipschitz dependence on the data in the $H^2$ norm, uniformly on bounded subsets of $H^3$ and compact time intervals, and joint locally Lipschitz dependence of $(t,f)\mapsto S(t)f$ into $L^2$; the classical conservation laws extend the flow globally in time.
item.dc:creator: Comlan Edmond Koudjinan

item.title: Local Optimality of the d-cube for Laplacian Eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2610.30463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each $d \ge 2$ we prove that the unit $d$-cube $\square_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is, on the class $\mathcal{P}$ of convex polytopes combinatorially equivalent to a $d$-cube, (i) a strict local minimizer of the scale-invariant isoperimetric ratio $I(\Omega) = \tfrac{P(\Omega)^d}{|\Omega|^{d-1}}$, with $P$ the perimeter, (ii) a strict local minimizer of the volume-normalized first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\bar\lambda(\Omega) = |\Omega|^{2/d}\lambda_1(\Omega)$, and (iii) a strict local maximizer of the volume-normalized first Neumann eigenvalue $\bar\mu(\Omega) = |\Omega|^{2/d}\mu_1(\Omega)$. The method is a shape-derivative Hessian analysis adapted to the hyperoctahedral symmetry of the cube. In symmetry-adapted coordinates on the parameter space --- the decomposition into irreducible representations of the hyperoctahedral group --- each Hessian is block-diagonal, with four scalar eigenvalues, which we give in closed form in $\pi$, rational coefficients, and a few universal series-constants. The first Neumann eigenvalue is not differentiable at $\square_d$, since its lowest cluster splits under perturbation. The Neumann case therefore works with a smooth auxiliary functional, whose Hessian is computed by second-order perturbation theory of the cluster; the coupling to modes outside the cluster enters at the same order. Finally, we show that extremality of $I$, $\bar\lambda$, and $\bar\mu$ does not hold in high dimensions for a particular multilinear perturbation that leaves $\mathcal{P}$ by breaking convexity. All results are local; we discuss why a global statement, available for quadrilaterals (Endo and Osting, 2026), appears out of reach for $d \ge 3$.
item.dc:creator: Braxton Osting, Robert Viator

item.title: Discovery of Singularities in Partial Differential Equations Using Adaptive Numerical Discretizations
item.description: arXiv:2610.30492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute self-similar singularity profiles of partial differential equations (PDEs) using adaptive numerical discretizations based on optimizing a discrete loss (ODIL). The fields are represented in overlapping local Chebyshev patches joined with a mapped asymptotic patch. After factoring out the leading power laws of solution ansatzes, their limiting amplitudes at infinity are determined by the optimization, eliminating domain truncation and prescribed far-field conditions. Adaptive refinement is guided by Chebyshev-coefficient decay, and the nonlinear least-squares problem is solved using automatically differentiated Gauss--Newton iterations with Levenberg--Marquardt damping. The method achieves O(10^{-14})-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^{-14}) to O(10^{-10}) for the generalized De Gregorio family, and of O(10^{-8}) in a local region for the two-dimensional Boussinesq equations. These results demonstrate that ODIL can identify singularity profiles for PDEs with high accuracy using adaptive numerical methods, complementing ongoing efforts that rely on artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Allen Yang, Lucas Amoudruz, Petros Koumoutsakos

item.title: Entropy bounded compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for hyperbolic conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2610.30496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we introduce a compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for the Euler equations of compressible gas dynamics, which preserves a minimum entropy principle similar to that introduced by Tadmor for entropy solution of the Euler equations [4]. Compact stencil RKDG, introduced by Chen et al. in [15], is a variant of standard RKDG method which is known for its smaller stencil size and parallel efficiency. The main challenge is that the cRKDG method has to be expressed in Butcher form and not every Runge-Kutta method of this form is a convex combination of forward-Euler steps. Therefore, in order to establish this property we leverage the bound preserving framework of the cRKDG schemes [8], an entropy bounded limiter [6] and the classical positivity preserving limiter. In the last section numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the robustness of the method.
item.dc:creator: Deepak Kumar, Pratima Rai, Arvind Patel

item.title: From Turing Patterns to Spike Self-Replication and Nucleation in a Growing-Domain Tulip Breaking Virus Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.30855v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A recently proposed reaction-diffusion model for the tulip breaking virus (TBV) has been shown to generate striped pigmentation patterns on growing tulip petals. In this paper, we investigate the formation of localized spike patterns in this model in the asymptotic limit of small viral diffusivity. It is known that two distinct bifurcation mechanisms can occur which generate new spikes as the domain half-length $L$ slowly increases: spike self-replication and spike nucleation. Self-replication occurs through a saddle-node bifurcation of the inner spike core problem, whereas nucleation is associated with a fold of the nonlinear outer problem. Using matched asymptotic expansions, we derive critical conditions for these mechanisms and construct phase diagrams that predict which mechanism occurs first as $L$ increases, or whether nucleation is absent. We further combine these results with a Turing instability analysis of the homogeneous steady state to obtain a phase diagram of pattern-forming mechanisms. An interesting finding is that, for the TBV model, the Turing-unstable region lies entirely within the parameter regime where spike nucleation is possible. These results provide further insight into the mechanisms underlying the formation and evolution of pigmentation patterns in virus-infected tulips.
item.dc:creator: Fanya Xia, Chunyi Gai

item.title: The Keller-Segel Model for Chemotaxis on Metapopulation Graphs and Graphons
item.description: arXiv:2610.31049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many models of spatial populations use directed motion towards environmental attractants as a mechanism for spatial pattern formation. While prior approaches typically focus on partial differential equation models for directed motion in continuous space, it is natural to consider the dynamics of biological and social systems on a metapopulation featuring well-mixed local patches and spatial motion between patches. In this paper, we formulate a version of the Keller-Segel model for chemotaxis on a graph metapopulation, modeling a chemoattractant that can diffuse across patches and a population of individuals who move through a biased random walk through comparing chemoattractant levels along edges of the metapopulation network. We also derive a continuum limit for our model describing chemotaxis in a population on patches connected by a graphon, showing that our resulting integro-differential equation model arises as the limit of our discrete patch model for families of large deterministic or random graphs. Through linear stability analysis, we derive conditions on the chemotactic sensitivity required to produce instability of a spatially uniform equilibrium for our Keller-Segel models in terms of the reaction parameters and the eigenvalues of the Laplacian operator for the metapopulation graph or graphon. Through a mix of weakly nonlinear stability analysis, numerical simulations, and analytical bounds on solutions, we can also characterize the form of pattern-forming instability in our graphon model and show how our choice of demographic dynamics for the population and the graphon adjacency function can impact the long-time total population size and chemoattractant concentration achieved in emergent spatial patterns.
item.dc:creator: Daecheol Kim, Yefei Zhang, Yuxuan Zhao, Daniel B. Cooney

item.title: Complete conformal metrics of constant positive scalar curvature with prescribed isolated singularities
item.description: arXiv:2610.31058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with positive Yamabe constant. For any prescribed finite set $\Lambda\subset M$ containing at least two points, we construct a complete metric on $M\setminus\Lambda$, conformal to $g$, with scalar curvature $n(n-1)$. At each singularity, the local geometric term in the reduced action comes from the first nonzero homogeneous metric term of degree at most $(n-2)/2$ in finite conformal normal coordinates, or from the mass of the Green function metric when all such terms vanish. We completely solve Schoen's conjecture about singular Yamabe problem.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Chen, Li Ma

item.title: On global Chern-Calabi flows on compact complex surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31068v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose the Chern-Calabi Flow for extremal metrics in conformal Hermitian geometry. After the existence of extremal metric, we consider the existence of global flows to the Chern-Calabi flows for extremal metrics on compact complex surfaces with Gauduchon metrics. To achieve this goal, we use the Adams inequality and the Gronwall inequality method to obtain fourth order derivative norm estimates. We also study the convergence of the global solution to the Chern-Calabi flow and its limit is the solution of the Chern-Calabi extremal metric problem. We propose a fourth order elliptic problem and derive the Bochner formula relevant to the elliptic estimates for the Chern-Calabi heat flow.
item.dc:creator: Li Ma, Li Sheng

item.title: Sharp Variational estimates for Schr\"{o}dinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31099v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $p\geq2$ and $r\geq 1$, we prove the sharp strong $r$-variation estimate for solutions to the free Schr\"odinger equation $$ \bigl\|V^r_{[0,1]}\{e^{it\Delta}f\}\bigr\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)} \lesssim \|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^2)}. $$ The estimate holds if $s> s(p,r)$ and fails if $s< s(p,r)$, where $$s(p,r)=\max\left\{ \frac{2}{r}+\frac{1}{p}-\frac12,\, \frac{2}{r}-\frac{2}{p},\, \frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{r},\, \frac{2}{p}-\frac13,\, 1-\frac{2}{p} \right\}.$$ In particular, $s(3,\infty)=1/3$. Thus our result yields a sharp variational extension of the two-dimensional Schr\"odinger maximal estimate of Du, Guth, and Li [{Ann. Math.}, 186, 607--640 (2017)]. The proof employs fractal restriction estimates to eliminate the regularity loss originating from the summation in the variation norm.
item.dc:creator: Yanping Chen, Yongrui Tang

item.title: Hadamard states for linearized gravity on asymptotically flat spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.31214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the quantization of linearized Einstein equations on 4-dimensional asymptotically flat spacetimes. We prove the existence of fully gauge invariant Hadamard states in the harmonic gauge for any Einstein metric asymptotic to the Minkowski metric in a conic neighborhood of spatial infinity.
item.dc:creator: Christian G\'erard, Mikhail Molodyk, Micha{\l} Wrochna

item.title: Exact controllability and rapid stabilization of linear difference delay equations and one-dimensional hyperbolic systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper addresses exact controllability and rapid stabilization issues for linear difference delay systems with finitely many pointwise delays. We first establish a criterion for exact controllability in $L^r$, $r \in [1, +\infty)$, characterized by a necessary and sufficient Hautus-type frequency-domain condition. The sufficiency of this condition in $L^r$ was already known [https://hal.science/hal-04830757/], whereas its necessity had previously been established only in $L^1$ [arXiv:2210.13590]. We answer [arXiv:2210.13590, Conjecture 3.8] by proving that this condition is also necessary for $r \in (1, +\infty)$. The analysis is based on rewriting the system as an evolution equation in a suitable Banach space, which allows one to apply duality arguments in the spirit of [https://doi.org/10.1137/S036301299119795X]. Building on this controllability analysis and the abstract stabilization framework developed in [https://doi.org/10.1137/S0363012996301609, arXiv:1301.5744], we prove that our exact controllability criterion in $L^r$ is also a sufficient condition for rapid stabilization in $L^2$, i.e., that the system of interest can be stabilized by a family of state feedback control laws ensuring that the closed-loop system is exponentially stable in $L^2$ with an arbitrarily large decay rate. As an application, we extend our results to linear one-dimensional hyperbolic partial differential equations, which can be reduced to linear difference delay systems via the method of characteristics, obtaining also a necessary and sufficient frequency-domain criterion for exact controllability in $L^r$, $r\in [1, +\infty)$, which, as before, is a sufficient condition for rapid stabilization in $L^2$.
item.dc:creator: Yacine Chitour, S\'ebastien Fueyo, Pierre Lissy, Guilherme Mazanti

item.title: Continuation and convergence for the higher dimensional conformal Chern--Calabi flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.31270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the volume-normalized gradient flow of the squared Chern scalar curvature on compact Hermitian manifolds of complex dimension $n\ge3$. The flow extends smoothly past a finite time if the spatial supremum of Chern scalar curvature belongs to $L^2$ in time. A uniform curvature bound in the evolving $L^p$ norm, for one fixed $p>n$, gives global existence and smooth convergence of the whole trajectory to a constrained critical metric. On Chern scalar-flat backgrounds, small initial $L^p$ curvature gives exponential convergence to the background. A corresponding condition on the trace-free first Chern--Ricci form gives exponential convergence on Chern--Ricci-flat Hermitian and positive K\"ahler--Einstein backgrounds. The smallness thresholds are independent of the initial higher derivatives. We also construct constant Chern scalar curvature backgrounds of either sign with arbitrarily small smooth perturbations whose solutions, if global, cannot converge back to the background.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Chen, Li Ma, Li Sheng

item.title: Numerical reconstruction of polygonal obstacles by diffracted waves
item.description: arXiv:2610.31271v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a numerical method for recovering rigid polygonal obstacles in two dimensions, based on the diffraction-based inverse scattering theory of Bao, Chen, Lu, and Xiong. A single pulse is emitted from a point source, and the resulting wave field is measured on a receiver curve. After isolating the diffracted signals, we recover the visible vertices from arrival times and the corner orientations and opening angles from amplitudes. The use of amplitude information permits local reconstruction in the reflection shadow, where reflected waves do not reach the receiver. The amplitudes also determine the direction of a shadowed edge adjacent to a visible vertex, enabling local non-line-of-sight imaging. Numerical experiments for a convex corner, a concave corner, a triangle, a pentagon and a star-shaped obstacle confirm that the visible portion of the boundary can be recovered stably from diffracted signals. A further convex-corner test with additive noise at level $0.2\%$ on the single arc $L_1$ confirms that the tip and opening remain recoverable.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen, Kuangmiao Xiong, Boxi Xu

item.title: Lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions for a class of curvilinear polygons
item.description: arXiv:2610.31387v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Steklov eigenfunctions, $\{\phi_{\sigma_j}\}_{j=0}^\infty$, are the eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet to Neumann map on a bounded domain with eigenvalue $\sigma_j$. This paper considers Steklov eigenfunctions and eigenvalues on a family of curvilinear polygons, $\Omega_\alpha$ whose boundaries are smooth away from a single corner of angle $\alpha$. We (i) prove optimal lower bounds on the decay of the harmonic extension, $u_{\sigma_j}$, of $\phi_{\sigma_j}$ away from the boundary of $\Omega_\alpha$ and (ii) give optimal lower bounds on the degree to which the high energy Steklov spectrum of $\Omega_\alpha\setminus H_1$ may differ from that of $\Omega_\alpha\setminus H_0$ when $H_1$ and $H_0$ are isometric. This shows that the corresponding estimates in recent work by the authors together with Malagutti are optimal. The proof in this paper was obtained through an interaction with ChatGPT 6 Astra: While writing the work with Malagutti, the authors became curious about optimal error bounds for the difference between the Steklov spectra on a curvilinear polygon, $P$, and the spectrum of any operator which knows only local information about $\partial P$. The authors suggested to ChatGPT to remove two isometric, smooth domains from a curvilinear polygon. ChatGPT suggested the ideas for a proof based on a regularized trace and the singularity in the kernel of the DtN map near a corner. The authors then suggested a simpler, conformal approach, the method for handling small angles, and the idea to obtain lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions. The paper is entirely written by the authors and the argument has been significantly modified, clarified, and simplified from the ChatGPT ideas.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Galkowski, Ruoyu P. T. Wang

item.title: Concavity-Free $L^\infty$ Estimates and Stability for Fully Nonlinear Complex Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.31453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we extend the $L^\infty$ estimates of Guo-Phong for fully non-linear equations on compact hermitian manifolds to a possibly indefinite reference form satisfying a uniform admissibility criterion. Furthermore, we also establish one-sided stability estimates. Neither result requires homogeneity or concavity of the nonlinear operator.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mc Gowan

item.title: P\'olya's conjecture for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells
item.description: arXiv:2610.31464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the strict P\'olya inequality for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells in every dimension $d\ge2$, for every radius ratio and every positive energy. The proof also covers balls. For shells, the excess over the leading Weyl term has a positive lower bound depending only on dimension. Above explicit frequency thresholds independent of the radius ratio, we obtain a surplus of boundary order. These estimates remain uniform as the hole shrinks or the shell becomes thin. We compare weighted sampling errors for inverse radial actions while retaining the removed volume exactly. The proof is entirely analytic and requires no computer-assisted verification.
item.dc:creator: Yutian Li

item.title: A sharpened $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate for even initial data
item.description: arXiv:2610.31543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is well known that $u_0 \in L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ is an extremizer for the $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate if and only if it is a Gaussian. We show that every extremizing sequence of even functions $\{ u_n \} \subset L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ approaches a centered Gaussian in an appropriate sense. This result follows from a certain inequality for coordinate-wise even $L^2$ functions on $\mathbb{R}^4$ conjectured by Gon\c{c}alves (2019) which we prove in this paper with the optimal constant.
item.dc:creator: Soichiro Suzuki

item.title: SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.31600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The attention mechanism underpins modern large language models, yet their dynamics remain only partially understood. Recent perspectives interpret attention blocks as interacting particle systems, whose mean-field limits correspond to gradient flows of energy functionals on spaces of probability densities on $\mathbb R^d$ equipped with Wasserstein-type metrics. We extend this viewpoint by deriving accelerated attention blocks from inertial, Nesterov-type damped Hamiltonian dynamics on these density spaces, developing the geometry and differential calculus needed to make the construction rigorous. In particular, we introduce a local-mobility geometry for the Otto-Wasserstein and softmax-Wasserstein settings, and a quotient Stein geometry that resolves the degeneracy of the linear-attention kernel to yield a well-defined metric and differential calculus. We provide rigorous foundations when softmax attention admits a gradient-flow formulation and when its inertial counterpart admits a damped Hamiltonian on explicitly characterized domains. For linear attention, we obtain a finite-dimensional solution theory with sharp conditions for global existence versus finite-time second-moment blow-up. We further prove a quantitative link between continuous moment blow-up and the discrete-layer depth at which token norms cross a prescribed threshold. Finally, motivated by the finite-token geometry, we propose geometric corrections to token and momentum updates. In decoder-only, nanoGPT-style experiments on TinyStories and OpenWebText, these corrections lower validation negative log-likelihood on next-token prediction relative to momentum-only controls.
item.dc:creator: Viktor Stein, Levin Maier, Wuchen Li, Gabriele Steidl

item.title: Mean-field limit of non-exchangeable multi-agent systems over hypergraphs with unbounded rank
item.description: arXiv:2406.04691v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Interacting particle systems are known for their ability to generate large-scale self-organized structures from simple local interaction rules between each agent and its neighbors. In addition to studying their emergent behavior, a main focus of the mathematical community has been concentrated on deriving their large-population limit. In particular, the mean-field limit consists of describing the limit system by its population density in the product space of positions and labels. The strategy to derive such limits is often based on a careful combination of methods ranging from analysis of PDEs and stochastic analysis, to kinetic equations and graph theory. In this article, we focus on a generalization of multi-agent systems that includes higher-order interactions, which has largely captured the attention of the applied community in the last years. In such models, interactions between individuals are no longer assumed to be binary (i.e. between a pair of particles). Instead, individuals are allowed to interact by groups so that a full group jointly generates a non-linear force on any given individual. The underlying graph of connections is then replaced by a hypergraph, which we assume to be dense, but possibly non uniform and of unbounded rank. For the first time in the literature, we show that when the interaction kernels are regular enough, then the mean-field limit is determined by a limiting Vlasov-type equation, where the hypergraph limit is encoded by a so-called UR-hypergraphon (unbounded-rank hypergraphon), and where the resulting mean-field force admits infinitely-many orders of interactions.
item.dc:creator: Nathalie Ayi (SU), Nastassia Pouradier Duteil (MAMBA, MUSCLEES), David Poyato (UGR)

item.title: The linearized Israel-Stewart equations with a physical vacuum boundary
item.description: arXiv:2411.00291v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we consider the Israel-Stewart equations of relativistic viscous fluid dynamics with bulk viscosity. We investigate the evolution of the equations linearized about solutions that satisfy the physical vacuum boundary condition and establish local well-posedness of the corresponding Cauchy problem.
item.dc:creator: Runzhang Zhong

item.title: Existence and concentration of multiple solutions for the fractional logarithmic Schr\"odinger-Poisson system via the penalization method
item.description: arXiv:2508.16229v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study positive solutions of the fractional logarithmic Schr\"odinger-Poisson system \[ \begin{cases} \varepsilon^{2\alpha}(-\Delta)^\alpha u+V(x)u+\phi u=u\log u^2+|u|^{q-2}u, & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^3, \varepsilon^{2\alpha}(-\Delta)^\alpha \phi=u^2, & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^3, \end{cases} \] where \(\varepsilon>0\), \(3/4<\alpha<1\), and \(4<q<6/(3-2\alpha)\). We assume that the potential is continuous and nonnegative and attains its global minimum inside a bounded domain, with strictly larger values on the boundary. We work in the intersection of a weighted fractional Sobolev space and an Orlicz space, so that the logarithmic energy is finite and the associated functional is of class \(C^1\). For sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\), we obtain at least as many distinct positive solutions as the relative Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of the minimum set in a small neighborhood. The global maximum points of these solutions approach that minimum set as \(\varepsilon\to0\). The proof combines penalization, an autonomous Nehari-Pohozaev argument, a local natural constraint, and category theory.
item.dc:creator: Jiao Luo, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: Gamma Convergence and Smooth Exact-segregation Approximation for Partially Segregated Systems
item.description: arXiv:2510.03794v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study three-component Dirichlet energies subject to the partial segregation constraint \(u_1u_2u_3=0\). Our main result is a smooth approximation theorem on bounded Lipschitz domains in arbitrary dimension. For compatible nonnegative Lipschitz boundary data, every admissible \(H^1\) configuration can be approximated strongly in \(H^1\) by globally Lipschitz maps that are smooth in the interior and preserve both the prescribed boundary trace and the segregation constraint exactly. The construction combines a Lipschitz retraction, variable-radius mollification, and smooth truncation preserving existing zeros, without assumptions on interfaces or junctions. Under the weaker assumption of compatible nonnegative \(H^{1/2}\) boundary data, we establish existence of minimizers and \(\Gamma\)-convergence in \(L^2\) for the energies with product penalization \(\varepsilon^{-1}\int_\Omega(u_1u_2u_3)^2\,dx\). We also identify the exact \(L^2\) distance to the constrained class and construct segregated corrections with controlled Dirichlet energy. The resulting correction estimate has order \(\varepsilon^{1/6}\) for bounded-energy configurations; this exponent is sharp in general and improves to \(o(\varepsilon^{1/6})\) for almost-minimizers.
item.dc:creator: Farid Bozorgnia, Avetik Arakelyan

item.title: Capillary John ellipsoid theorem with applications to capillary curvature problems
item.description: arXiv:2603.27252v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we apply a capillary John ellipsoid theorem for capillary convex bodies in the Euclidean half-space $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_{+}}$. This theorem yields a non-collapsing estimate for capillary hypersurfaces, which provides a new approach to obtaining $C^{0}$ estimates for solutions to some capillary curvature problems (including the capillary $L_{p}$ Christoffel-Minkowski problem and the capillary $L_{p}$ curvature problem), based on the corresponding gradient estimates. As an application, we study the capillary $L_{p}$ dual Minkowski problem. A gradient estimate, together with the non-collapsing estimate and a $C^2$ estimate, yields existence for every $1<p<q<\infty$ with positive smooth even data and an acute contact angle. The same estimates also yield the eigenvalue problem for $p=q>1$, with uniqueness up to dilation. We further obtain existence and uniqueness for $p>q$ without an upper restriction on $q$.
item.dc:creator: Jinrong Hu, Yingxiang Hu, Bo Yang

item.title: Short-wave signal versus indirect prey-taxis
item.description: arXiv:2604.20469v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We address a short-wave asymptotic for one class of quasi-linear second-order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak-Keller-Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modeling the predator-prey community with the prey-taxis, which means the interactions of two species of particles or cells or anything else through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a cue produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the cue is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent of the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete formal asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions (modulo solving a chain of the so-called slow systems) with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter- or intra-specific reactions. Further, we apply the short-wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza's theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes of external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of the robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal up to a very strong stabilization or, oppositely, destabilization, and something like blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Morgulis, Karrar Malal

item.title: On nonnegative solutions of the differential inequality $\Delta_pu+ \Delta_q u+V(x)u^s\leq 0$ on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2604.23624v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with differential inequalities with $(p,q)$-Laplacian operator on Riemannian manifolds. Using a test function argument, we establish Liouville-type theorems under the manifold's geometry and the potential's behavior at infinity. Finally, we give an example showing the sharpness when $V(x)$ is a positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Biqiang Zhao

item.title: Inhomogeneous NLS in negative Sobolev spaces via Fourier-Lebesgue and modulation spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.30777v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The purpose of this work is to provide a broader framework for analyzing the 1D mass-subcritical inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (INLS) \[iu_t + u_{xx} \pm |x|^{-b}|u|^{\alpha-1}u=0, \quad 1<\alpha< 5-2b\; \text{and}\; 0< b\leq 1/4.\] in Sobolev spaces of negative order, reaching almost critical Sobolev spaces by working in Fourier-Lebesgue and modulation spaces. More precisely, we establish low-regularity well-posedness in the Fourier-Lebesgue $\widehat{L}^{p}$ spaces for $4/3<p<8$. Primarily, we prove global well-posedness for arbitrarily large initial data via the data decomposition method adapted for the Fourier-Lebesgue spaces, with generalized Strichartz estimates for $p<2$ and classical Strichartz estimates for $p>2$. Furthermore, we obtain analogous results for (INLS) in modulation spaces $M^{p,p'}$ for $4/3<p<2$.
item.dc:creator: Divyang G. Bhimani, Diksha Dhingra, Vijay Kumar Sohani

item.title: New link between the fractional p-Laplacian operators and a class of McKean-Vlasov flight type processes
item.description: arXiv:2609.19492v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence of a McKean--Vlasov stochastic process with jumps associated to the nonlinear parabolic equation $\partial_t u = \Delta_p u + \Delta_p^s u$ in $\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty)$, where $\Delta_p$ is the $p$-Laplacian and $\Delta_p^s$ is the fractional $p$-Laplacian. Our approach is the following: first, after proving the existence of a solution for the PDE presented earlier, we rewrite it as a nonlinear Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation whose measure-valued solution is guaranteed when $p\ge4$. Then we solve the martingale problem associated to our FPKE via a new superposition principle for non-local Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equations, which only requires an integrability condition on the local coefficients. Finally, thanks to the martingale solution obtained, we derive the existence of a weak solution for the McKean-Vlasov's type SDE with jumps whose infinitesimal generator is a << hybrid version >> of the operator $\Delta_p+\Delta_p^s$.
item.dc:creator: Houssine El Jeddaoui, Dany Nabab

item.title: On wave operators for Hardy operators with and without perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2610.08594v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove asymptotic completeness of the wave operators in time-dependent scattering theory which intertwine the ordinary or fractional Laplacian and the corresponding Hardy operator, i.e., the fractional Laplacian with an added subcritical or critical Hardy potential, whenever the Hardy potential is short-range. Moreover, we prove asymptotic completeness of the wave operators intertwining Hardy operators with and without external short-range perturbations. We also show the nonexistence of the considered wave operators when the Hardy or external potentials are long-range. We arrive at these results using three different approaches. The first approach uses an abstract semigroup framework for asymptotic completeness of wave operators for Fourier multipliers with short-range potentials. The second approach uses Kato smoothness theory. In the third approach, we develop and apply new propagation estimates for Hardy operators with and without perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Atsuhide Ishida, Konstantin Merz

item.title: Interior gradient estimates for mean curvature equations on Riemannian manifolds
item.description:
arXiv:2610.24745v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study interior gradient estimates for solutions of \[ \operatorname{div}_{M}\left(  rac{
abla u}{\sqrt{1+|
abla u|_g^2}} ight) =f(x,
abla u) \] on a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge2$. Under a Ricci curvature lower bound and a Hessian comparison for the distance function, we derive polynomial and exponential gradient bounds under structural conditions on $f$ and its horizontal and vertical derivatives. The estimates quantify the dependence on the radius, the oscillation of the solution, and the geometric and analytic parameters. In the Euclidean case, we also improve the dependence on the radius in the gradient estimate of Xu~\cite[Theorem~1.1(d)]{Xu2026}. As applications, we obtain Liouville-type results for entire solutions under suitable curvature and growth assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Weiyang Li, Fanheng Xu

item.title: Minimality and stability of the ball for the charge-qubit energy
item.description: arXiv:2610.27218v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the shape optimization problem introduced by Mazzoleni, Muratov, and Ruffini as a model for a superconducting charge qubit, in which the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of a set of prescribed volume competes with the Coulomb self-energy of the ground state. We prove that, for sufficiently small charge, the ball is the unique minimizer, and that the energy deficit of a volume-preserving and centered perturbation of the ball is comparable to the squared $H^{1/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, with constants independent of the charge. We also obtain the corresponding results for the quadratic Hartree--Ohta--Kawasaki model.
item.dc:creator: Ihsan Topaloglu

item.title: A min-max gap characterization of minimal foliations on the torus
item.description: arXiv:2605.12428v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend an energy introduced by Mather to the setting of Almgren-Pitts min-max theory and obtain a parametric, higher-dimensional analogue of Mather's variational barrier theory for twist maps and geodesics on tori. We use this energy to establish several criteria for the existence of foliations of the $n$-torus by minimal hypersurfaces. We show that for a generic metric, whenever a lamination by area-minimizing hypersurfaces of the $n$-torus contains a gap, there exists a minimal hypersurface inside the gap that is not area-minimizing. This hypersurface is a higher-dimensional analogue of the secondary minimax orbit appearing in Aubry-Mather theory.
item.dc:creator: Hoan Nguyen

item.title: A general paracontrolled ansatz for singular SPDEs
item.description: arXiv:2608.09700v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a general ansatz for the paracontrolled approach introduced by Gubinelli, Imkeller, Perkowski for treating singular SPDEs. The ansatz proposed covers a large class of equations. It is described via decorated trees that encode its coefficients and its stochastic data. The main novelty is the recursive definition of the paracontrolled stochastic iterated integrals that involve a well-chosen combinatorial set of words. The paralinearisation is performed via a lift of iterated paraproducts to modelled distributions. The main idea is to integrate localised iterated paraproducts in order to get a global object with a good regularity. We also provide a fixed point argument and the renormalised equation with this ansatz when one uses the preparation map formalism that encompasses the BPHZ renormalisation. The last main result is the convergence of the renormalised stochastic data via the BPHZ renormalisation using an adaptation of the spectral gap approach. One obtains in the end a general solution theory for parabolic singular SPDEs via the paracontrolled approach.
item.dc:creator: Yvain Bruned, Nicolas Moench

item.title: Jacobian estimates and geometric inequalities under intermediate Ricci curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.13690v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a Jacobian estimate underlying both the Heintze--Karcher comparison and the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci method for submanifolds of arbitrary codimension. The estimate retains the contributions of ambient curvature along geodesics emanating from the submanifold and requires no curvature sign assumption. As applications, we obtain a quantitative Fenchel--Willmore inequality with explicit curvature remainders under nonnegative $n$-intermediate Ricci curvature, Michael--Simon Sobolev and isoperimetric inequalities under nonnegative $(n-1)$-intermediate Ricci curvature, and corresponding extensions under quadratic curvature decay. In each result, the required intermediate Ricci curvature condition depends only on the dimension of the submanifold and is independent of its codimension.
item.dc:creator: Kwok-Kun Kwong, Jihye Lee, Fabio Ricci
